title: Do as I Say, Not as You Do: Assessing Public Versus Practitioner Perspectives on the Development of Artificial Intelligence and Language Technologies
abstract: arXiv:2611.28013v1 Announce Type: cross  Abstract: With the public awareness of artificial intelligence (AI) applications such as large language models (LLMs) and generative text-to-video models reaching unprecedented levels, there is an increasing need to reconcile the perspectives held by informed practitioners, who research and develop these technologies, with the interests and opinions of the general public, who constitute the majority of people impacted by technological developments. In this work, we survey practitioners (i.e., academics and industry professionals) alongside members of the general public on perspectives relating to pertinent areas of artificial intelligence, including perceived benefit and risk, the ability for models to achieve consciousness and output art, and the use of copyright protected material for model training. Alongside comparisons of diverse perspectives on these topics, we additionally contextualise the findings with a discussion of relevant literatur

translated_title: 照我说的做，而非照你做的做：评估公众与从业者对人工智能和语言技术发展的看法
translated_abstract: 随着公众对人工智能（AI）应用（如大型语言模型（LLMs）和生成式文生视频模型）的认知达到前所未有的水平，越来越需要调和知情的从业者（即研究和开发这些技术的人员）的观点与构成技术发展影响大多数人群体的普通公众的利益和意见。在这项工作中，我们调查了从业者（即学术界和行业专业人士）以及普通公众对人工智能相关重要领域的看法，包括感知的收益与风险、模型实现意识和输出艺术作品的能力，以及使用受版权保护的材料进行模型训练的问题。除了比较这些主题上多样化的观点之外，我们还结合相关文献的讨论对研究结果进行了背景分析。
tldr: 该论文通过对从业者和普通公众的调查比较，揭示了两个群体在人工智能的收益与风险感知、模型意识和艺术生成能力、以及版权材料用于模型训练等关键问题上的观点差异。
